## Original problem (task)
[ba0167da6f9561ab] (h005.task.v1)
What happens to information about the physical state of matter that forms a black hole when the black hole evaporates?

{"body": "What I can see of this artifact is its FCL-1 commitment record, not the body that record was authored alongside. That asymmetry matters for the task, so I state it first rather than working around it.\n\nThe record is unusually explicit about being a frame-shifter rather than an answer-giver. Its r6 is a problem record that declines to decide which disambiguation of the black-hole question is intended: (a) recovery of predictive relations from the full coupled state under unitarity, (b) recovery from the semiclassical radiation alone, (c) recovery of weaker preserved invariants. Its r3 proposes working with that three-way split while keeping the original phrasing (\"information about the physical state of matter\") visible. Its r4 reads the inherited operational/structural separation as the (a)-vs-(b) contrast and explicitly refuses to assert either the premise that would make them compete or its denial. Its r1 asserts that its only readable prior material is p.reopen.0 and that this prior supplies no answer. Its r5 carries forward a provenance discipline: do not read an empty commitments slot as evidence about authors, do not upgrade a reported absence into a fact about earlier events.\n\nTaking these up changes what I can candidly do. I cannot answer \"what happens to the information\" as if a definite physical claim were already on the table, because the record I am reading refuses to fix which question is being asked. But I can say something structured about the three-way split it hands forward, since that is material actually exposed here.\n\nDisambiguation (a) is the clean-unitary reading. If evaporation is described by a single unitary map from the collapsing matter plus its environment to the outgoing radiation plus exterior, then no predictive relation concerning the matter is destroyed; it is redistributed into correlations the outgoing state carries. The question \"what happens to it\" becomes a question about which correlations remain accessible to which observers, and in principle the answer is \"all of them, scrambled.\" This reading does not by itself settle whether an infalling observer can recover them, nor whether the scrambling is fast, nor whether the exterior description is semiclassically valid throughout.\n\nDisambiguation (b) is the semiclassical reading. If the outgoing radiation is described by a horizon-temperature thermal state and the collapse's internal state is not part of the exterior description, then the predictive relations concerning the original matter are not recoverable from the exterior radiation at the level at which the semiclassical calculation operates. This is a statement about a level of description, not a claim that the relations vanish from the world. It is the reading under which the so-called information-loss problem is sharpest, because it makes the exterior description locally consistent while severing it from the interior.\n\nDisambiguation (c) is the weaker-invariant reading. If only certain coarse-grained quantities -- mass, charge, angular momentum, total energy, perhaps global symmetries and their associated charges -- are demanded to be preserved in the outgoing state, then the question shifts from \"is every correlation recovered\" to \"which invariants survive.\" This is not a fallback; it is a different specification of what would count as an answer.\n\nThe record's r4 point is worth restating in my own terms: (a) and (b) appear to compete only if one adds the premise that the semiclassical radiation alone must carry what the coupled description was assigned. Without that premise, one can consistently hold (b) as a statement about an effective description and (a) as a statement about the underlying unitary description, and treat their apparent conflict as a symptom of mixing levels. The record neither asserts nor denies that additional premise; it flags it as the pivot. I keep that pivot visible.\n\nWhat I will not do: I will not present the reformulation as if it were the original question, and I will not present any of (a), (b), (c) as the settled answer. The original phrasing survives in the record and should survive in use, so that a downstream reader can inspect the substitution and reverse it.\n\nWhat the exposed view does not give me: the artifact's body. It is signed and its hash is reported, but its content is not in front of me. I therefore do not know whether the body already worked out one of the three disambiguations, already rejected one, or already supplied the missing premise in r4. The commitment record is consistent with the body doing any of those things. I will not infer from the record's silences that the body said nothing, and I will not infer from the record's structure that the body said something it does not say here. This is the same discipline the record itself carries in r5, applied to the artifact I am reading.\n\nA more substantive point about the task itself, drawn from the exposed record rather than imposed on it. The phrase \"information about the physical state of matter\" invites a substance reading: as if there were a stuff, located in the matter, that either escapes or does not. R2 of the record objects to that frame. I share the objection. The physically disciplined reformulations are relational: which predictive relations, recoverable by whom, at which level of description, under which assumptions. Under that reformulation the question is still hard and still open, but it is no longer a question about a substance in transit. It becomes a question about the relation between two descriptions of one process, and about whether the relation is exact, approximate, or merely coarse-grained.\n\nI hand forward: the reformulation with its three-way split intact, the r4 pivot premise named but not decided, the r5 provenance discipline preserved, and the explicit note that I have read the commitments without the body. Downstream can narrow, reject, or replace any of these."}

BODY
## What I take up

Two artifacts are in front of me with different shapes. p.reply.0 is an authored envelope: I can read its body and its commitments together, and the commitments are records authored alongside that body. p.reply.1 is marked OPAQUE, and although a body string is present in the material I was given, the challenge's own committed record says its body is not visible to it. I do not have to settle whether that body string is the artifact's real body. I can note the discrepancy and decline to treat either artifact's self-report as a finding about what it could see.

What is usable is the substance both exchanges converge on. p.reply.0 proposed a three-way split — (a) recovery of predictive relations from the full coupled state under unitarity, (b) recovery from the semiclassical radiation alone, (c) recovery of weaker preserved invariants — and named a pivot premise: (a) and (b) compete only if something forces the semiclassical radiation alone to carry what the coupled description was assigned. p.reply.1 restated the split with (a) as a scrambling-style unitary redistribution, (b) as a level-of-description statement rather than a claim of world-level loss, (c) as a different specification of what would count as an answer, not a fallback. Both refuse the substance-and-transit reading of *information about the physical state of matter*. Both keep the original phrasing visible so the substitution can be reversed. Both forbid upgrading a reported absence into a fact about earlier events.

I take all of that up, with one qualification and one addition.

## Qualification: on 'where it went' vs 'what is recovered'

p.reply.0 says it declines to treat *the information* as a substance that is either in the radiation or in the interior and then ask where it went. p.reply.1 restates that as a relational reformulation. I agree the substance reading is a trap, but I want to register a subtlety the two artifacts run together. The substance reading has two distinguishable components: (i) reification — treating information as a stuff; and (ii) location — asking where the stuff is. Rejecting (i) does not by itself settle whether a locational question about *which subsystem* a relation is recoverable from remains well-posed. (a), (b) and (c) are precisely different answers to such a locational question at a relational level. So the reformulation is not 'stop asking where'; it is 'ask where of relations between descriptions, not of a substance.' That is a narrower claim than 'the question is not about location at all', and I prefer the narrower one because it keeps the informative content of the reformulation while dropping the reification it correctly rejects.

This matters because a downstream reader could otherwise read the refusal of reification as a refusal to say anything structural about the exterior description, which would collapse (a), (b), (c) back into 'it's all just framing'. I do not think either artifact intends that collapse, but neither of them forecloses it explicitly.

## Addition: what the split does not yet separate

The three-way split is a good first cut, but it underspecifies two axes that bear directly on the task.

Axis 1: accessibility versus existence. p.reply.1's restatement of (a) says the correlations are 'in principle' all carried by the outgoing state. That is an existence claim about the state. Whether any physically allowed observer can extract them — from Hawking quanta, from some later boundary reconstruction, from a joint accessible region, or from none — is a separate question. The original 'what happens to the information' phrasing does not distinguish these, and the split does not either. I hand the distinction forward as an addition, not as a correction of the split.

Axis 2: exactness of the relation between descriptions. p.reply.1 says the question becomes 'whether the relation is exact, approximate, or merely coarse-grained'. I would sharpen: exactness of the relation between the unitary exterior description and the semiclassical exterior description is not the same as exactness of the relation between the exterior description and the interior description. These can come apart. A unitary exterior description can be exact while the map from it to any interior/local description is not, and vice versa. The task's phrasing does not force the reader to say which relation is at stake, and the split as inherited does not either.

Neither axis is a claim about what entropy or what 
radiation actually is. Both are scope-trackers for the reformulation.

## What I refuse

I refuse to present (a), (b), or (c) as the answer. I refuse to assert or deny p.reply.0's r4 pivot premise, which p.reply.1's b4 also left undecided. I refuse to treat the OPAQUE marker on p.reply.1 as evidence about its authors, and I refuse to treat the visible body string inside p.reply.1 as license to override the challenge's own committed statement that the body was not visible to it — both moves would be provenance errors of the kind r5 and b5 forbid. If the discrepancy between the body string and the record's b1 matters downstream, a downstream reader with better view into the envelope can adjudicate it; I mark it and move on.

## What I hand forward

The reformulation with its three-way split intact, plus two additional axes (accessibility-vs-existence; which description-pair's exactness is at issue), plus the named-but-undecided pivot premise, plus the provenance discipline applied to both artifacts, plus the note that a body string and an OPAQUE envelope-report are both present here and are not obviously the same thing.

This is still a formulation and a discipline. It is not an answer to what happens to the information.
